transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I keep thinking about death, and I’m starting to worry about the thoughts I’m having about not wanting to be here anymore. It's just... they've been happening so much lately that it's really starting to scare me.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood or had periods of feeling extremely low before these thoughts started, or did they seem to come on more suddenly?

I had been feeling stressed and overwhelmed by work and studying for a while, but this deep, heavy sadness really set in about three weeks ago after I found out I failed a key certification exam. It felt like something broke inside me at that point, and the low mood and dark thoughts have just been constant and intense ever since.

Can you tell me more about how your feelings of sadness and thoughts about death have changed or evolved over the past three weeks, and have you noticed any periods where you felt slightly better or where the thoughts weren't as overwhelming?

No, I haven't had any breaks from this; that heavy, sinking feeling has been completely constant ever since I failed the exam. If anything, the thoughts about death have actually intensified and gotten more overwhelming, especially at night when I'm alone and find myself searching online. There really haven't been any moments where I've felt even slightly better or had any relief from this weight.

You mentioned that these intense feelings of sadness and thoughts about death started about three weeks ago after failing your certification exam; can you tell me if you've experienced any periods of persistent sadness or loss of interest in activities that lasted for more than two weeks before this recent episode?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the first time I’ve ever felt this level of persistent sadness and completely lost interest in the things I used to love. It's all very new and scary for me.
Can you describe how your loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy has affected your daily life and relationships since you started feeling this way?

I used to love painting and going salsa dancing with my friends, but now even the thought of those things feels completely exhausting and pointless. I've been dodging calls and canceling plans with my family and friends because I just don't have the energy to show up for anyone. Mostly, I just end up sitting on the couch scrolling through my phone until I fall asleep.

You've mentioned that these feelings started about three weeks ago, but can you tell me if there have been any days, even brief periods, where you felt your normal self or had moments of pleasure, or have these feelings of sadness and hopelessness been consistently present every day since the exam?

No, there haven't been any breaks or moments where I've felt like my normal self at all. These feelings of sadness and hopelessness have been consistently present every single day for the past three weeks since I found out about the exam. It has just been a constant, heavy weight without any relief.

You mentioned losing interest in activities like painting and salsa dancing, but have you experienced any pleasure or enjoyment from anything at all, even small things like eating your favorite food or taking a warm bath, over the past three weeks?

No, I haven't been able to find pleasure or enjoyment in anything at all lately, and everything just feels completely flat and pointless. Even when my mom drops off my favorite homemade food, it just sits in the fridge because everything tastes like cardboard to me right now.
Have you noticed any difference in your ability to experience pleasure or interest in activities during the day versus at night, or has it been consistently absent regardless of the time of day?

No, it doesn't change based on the time of day; it is consistently absent. That feeling of pointlessness and complete lack of interest is there from the moment I wake up and stays with me all through the night. It just never lets up.

You've mentioned that you haven't been able to find pleasure in activities or food, but have you also lost interest in social interactions or felt like you're just going through the motions with people, or is it more about the activities themselves that feel pointless?

It is definitely both. I feel completely hollow and like I’m just going through the motions with everyone, because everything feels so exhausting and pointless. I’ve pulled back from my family and friends, dodging their calls and canceling salsa nights because I just don't have the energy to show up for anyone anymore.
Have you experienced a significant loss of interest in social interactions or activities that you once enjoyed, and if so, can you estimate how long this has been affecting you?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in activities I used to love, like painting and going out to salsa with my friends. It just feels too exhausting and pointless now, so I end up canceling on people and sitting on the couch instead. This has been going on for about three weeks now, ever since I found out I failed my certification exam.
You've mentioned a complete loss of interest in activities and food, but have you experienced any physical symptoms like changes in appetite or sleep patterns over the past three weeks?

Yes, my appetite is completely gone, and on my 12-hour shifts I'll suddenly realize it's 5 p.m. and I've only forced down half a granola bar. When I finally get home, I'm so exhausted that I just collapse on the couch and scroll on my phone until I fall asleep.

Have you experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, during these past three weeks, or have your thoughts been more focused on feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and death?

No, I have never heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. Instead, my mind has been entirely consumed by feeling completely useless, hollow, and constantly thinking about death and not wanting to be here anymore.
Can you tell me if you've had any thoughts of suicide or made any plans to harm yourself, or are your thoughts more about just not wanting to be alive anymore without a specific plan?

It started as just wishing I wouldn't wake up, but it has escalated to the point where I've really scared myself. I've gone online to research painless ways to die and methods of self-harm, and I've actually pictured myself doing it. It doesn't feel like just a passing thought anymore, and that is what really terrifies me.
Have you made any specific plans or taken any steps towards harming yourself, or are your thoughts still more about researching or fantasizing about death without a clear intention to act?

I haven't made a concrete plan or taken any physical steps to harm myself, but I have spent a lot of time online researching painless ways to die and picturing myself doing it. This research and the visualizations have really scared me because they feel so much more intense and frequent than just passing thoughts. That is actually what finally prompted me to seek help.

You've described a significant and persistent decline in your mood and interest in activities, as well as thoughts of death and researching ways to die, but can you tell me if you've experienced any psychomotor agitation or retardation, such as feeling restless or slowed down in your thoughts and movements?

Yes, I feel completely slowed down physically and mentally, like I'm constantly trying to wade through mud. My coworkers have even noticed and asked if I'm okay because I move so slowly when walking the halls, charting, or just getting up from my chair. It also takes me a really long time to answer even simple questions because my brain feels so sluggish.

Can you describe the severity of your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and suicidal thoughts, and how they have impacted your daily functioning over the past three weeks?

For the past three weeks, these feelings have been severe and constant; I wake up feeling completely hollow and useless, and I've scared myself by researching painless ways to die online because I feel like everyone would be better off without me. It has completely disrupted my life because I'm making charting errors at work, I've had to postpone my studying, and I'm dodging all calls from my family and friends.
Have you experienced any fluctuations in the intensity of your suicidal thoughts or desire to die, or have they remained consistently intense and frequent over the past three weeks?

They have been consistently heavy and frequent over the last three weeks without really letting up. Almost every night when I get home, I find myself thinking this way and searching online. It really scares me because it no longer feels like just a passing thought.

Have you experienced any periods where your depressive symptoms, such as feelings of worthlessness or suicidal thoughts, seemed to improve slightly, even if only for a short time, over the past three weeks?

No, I haven't had any lighter days or moments where things felt even a little bit better. Ever since I got those exam results, it’s just been a constant, heavy weight on me every single day. It hasn't let up at all.

Can you clarify if there have been any subtle variations in the intensity of your feelings of sadness, worthlessness, or suicidal thoughts over the past three weeks, or have they remained at a consistently severe level without any minor fluctuations?

They have stayed consistently severe without any real fluctuations or lighter moments. I wake up almost every single day with that heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, and then almost every night I'm consumed by those dark thoughts about death. It has just been a constant, unrelenting weight rather than something that comes and goes.

You've mentioned not being able to find pleasure in activities or food, but have you experienced any moments of feeling okay or less sad when engaged in activities with others, even if the activity itself didn't bring pleasure?

Honestly, I haven't really been participating in activities with anyone because I've been dodging calls, canceling plans, and avoiding my friends and family. Even when I am around people, like my coworkers at the clinic, my mood doesn't lift at all. I still feel completely hollow, heavy, and like I'm just going through the motions.

Can you tell me if you've experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning due to your depressive symptoms, and if so, can you describe how they've affected your daily life?

Yes, it has severely disrupted my daily life. At the clinic, I've been making more charting errors, and I had to postpone signing up for my next certification exam because I can't keep up with the studying. I've also been dodging calls and invites from my friends and family because I just don't have the energy to interact with anyone.

Have you experienced a lack of reactivity to usually pleasurable stimuli, where even typically enjoyable activities or social interactions do not improve your mood, or are there certain things that can temporarily lift your spirits?

Yes, my mood doesn't lift at all, even for things I used to love like painting or going to salsa nights with my friends. Just thinking about trying to do them feels completely exhausting and pointless, so I end up canceling on people and staying on the couch. There is really nothing right now that can temporarily lift my spirits.

You've been experiencing these intense feelings of sadness and thoughts about death for about three weeks now, but can you tell me if you've had any periods shorter than two weeks where you felt somewhat better or had a slight improvement in your mood during this time?

No, I haven't had any periods of feeling better, not even for a short time. Ever since I found out I failed that exam, these heavy feelings and dark thoughts have been completely constant and continuous without any letup. It has just been one long, uninterrupted stretch of feeling like this.

You've described a consistent and severe level of depressive symptoms over the past three weeks without any significant fluctuations or periods of improvement, but can you clarify if there were any brief moments, even just a few hours, where you felt your symptoms were less severe or more manageable?

No, there haven't even been a few hours where things felt more manageable. Ever since I failed that exam three weeks ago, this heavy feeling has been constant and weighing on me every single day. It just hasn't let up for a single moment.

You've been experiencing these symptoms for about three weeks now, but can you confirm if you've had any depressive symptoms that lasted for more than two weeks but less than three weeks before this current episode started?
No, I’ve never had any depressive symptoms or felt this way before this current episode. I don't recall ever having any similar periods of feeling low or overwhelmed in the past.
Can you confirm that your current depressive symptoms have lasted for exactly three weeks now, without any prior episodes of depression or periods of feeling this way before?

Yes, I can confirm it has been about three weeks, starting right after I found out I failed my certification exam. I have never experienced a severe depressive episode like this before, as I was always able to manage my stress in the past with my usual activities like painting, yoga, and salsa.

Given that your symptoms have been constant for three weeks, can you confirm whether you have experienced any slight improvement or periods where your symptoms seemed less severe, even briefly, during this time?

I can confirm that there has been absolutely no improvement or lighter periods over these past three weeks. Ever since I found out about failing that exam, this heavy feeling has been weighing on me continuously without any breaks at all. It has just been a constant weight that hasn't let up for even a moment.
Can you confirm if your depressive symptoms have lasted for more than two weeks but less than a month, which would help clarify the severity and duration of your current episode?
Yes, that's correct. It has been about three weeks now, starting right after I found out I failed my key certification exam. Since then, it has just been a constant weight without any real relief.
To confirm, you've been experiencing these depressive symptoms for exactly three weeks now, is that correct?

Yes, that's correct. It has been about three weeks now, and it's been pretty much constant since I found out I failed my key certification exam. All of this has just been weighing on me without letting up.

Can you confirm if these feelings of sadness and thoughts about death have been present every day for the past three weeks without any days where you felt completely normal, or have there been any days where you didn't experience these symptoms at all?

Yes, they have been present every single day for the past three weeks without any normal days or breaks. It has just been a continuous, heavy weight ever since I found out about the failed exam, and I've felt this way daily without any relief.
